record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: For a Gaussian-copula parameter p with 0<p<1 and p≠1/2, determine whether there exists a function χ_p: R → {-1, 1} such that the Gaussian-copula correlation function ψ(p,p;ρ) equals h_{χ_p}(ρ)=E[χ_p(X)χ_p(Y)] for every ρ in [-1,1] when (X,Y) is a centered bivariate normal vector with covariance matrix Σ_2(ρ); equivalently, determine whether this ψ(p,p;·) can satisfy the workflow’s SIGN condition through some sign-valued function χ_p.

evidence.quote: If we thouroughly overhaul the CCP function [− 1, 1] ∋ ρ ↦→ 2/π arcsin(ρ) we recognise that some knowledge of Gaussian copulas (i.e., finite-dimensional multivariate distribution functions of univariate marginals generated by the distribution function of Gaussian random vectors) and (the probabilistic version) of the Hermite polynomials might become very fruitful regarding our indicated search for different “ suitable” CCP functions.

(2-RP1) Prove whether there are p ∈ (− 1, 1) \ { 1/2} and functions χp : R −→ {− 1, 1} such that ψ(p, p; ρ) = hχp(ρ) = E[χp(X) χp(Y)] for all ρ ∈ [− 1, 1] and (X, Y ) ∼ N2(0, Σ 2(ρ)), so that the condition (SIGN) of our workflow is satisfied for hχp.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi$ denote the standard normal cumulative distribution function and, for $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $\Sigma_2(\rho)=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$. For $p\in(0,1)$, define the bivariate Gaussian copula correlation function
$$\psi(p,p;\rho)\;=\;\mathbb{P}\bigl(X\le \Phi^{-1}(p),\ Y\le \Phi^{-1}(p)\bigr)-p^2,$$
where $(X,Y)$ is a centered bivariate Gaussian vector with covariance matrix $\Sigma_2(\rho)$ (more precisely, $\psi(p,p;\rho)$ is the standard Gaussian-copula expression that, after centering and normalizing, encodes the Pearson correlation produced by the Gaussian copula at level $p$).

For any measurable function $\chi:\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,1\}$ define
$$h_\chi(\rho)\;=\;\mathbb{E}\bigl[\chi(X)\chi(Y)\bigr],\qquad (X,Y)\sim\mathcal{N}_2(0,\Sigma_2(\rho)).$$

Question: Does there exist a parameter $p\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}$ and a measurable sign-valued function $\chi_p:\mathbb{R}\to\{-1,1\}$ such that
$$\psi(p,p;\rho)\;=\;h_{\chi_p}(\rho)\quad\text{for every }\rho\in[-1,1]\,?$$

Equivalently, can the Gaussian-copula CCP function $\psi(p,p;\cdot)$ (for some $p\ne 1/2$) be realized as the correlation function $\rho\mapsto\mathbb{E}[\chi_p(X)\chi_p(Y)]$ of a $\{-1,1\}$-valued function of a standard normal variable?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned a related follow-up work on upper bounds for Grothendieck constants and CCP functions (arXiv:2305.04428) discussing the multivariate Gaussian copula in this framework, but no source explicitly resolving the sign-realization question for $\psi(p,p;\cdot)$ with $p\ne 1/2$ was found. The status of the problem appears to remain unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Upper bounds for Grothendieck constants, quantum correlation matrices and CCP functions
status_evidence.snippet: Applies the CCP framework to concrete examples including the multivariate Gaussian copula, within the search for the exact value of real/complex Grothendieck constants.
status_evidence.claim: Related follow-up work treats Gaussian-copula CCP functions but does not appear to settle the sign-realization question for p≠1/2.
